actions.reason: Apply ordered merge replacements directly in the str-based encode paths instead of first testing membership. str.replace already returns the unchanged string when the pair is absent, so this avoids an extra scan for pairs that are present while preserving the produced token ids.

candidate.patch:
diff --git a/minbpe/basic.py b/minbpe/basic.py
--- a/minbpe/basic.py
+++ b/minbpe/basic.py
@@ -161,8 +161,7 @@ class BasicTokenizer(Tokenizer):
             for pair, new, _ in steps:
                 if len(s) < 2:
                     break
-                if pair in s:
-                    s = s.replace(pair, new)
+                s = s.replace(pair, new)
             return [ord(c) for c in s]
         ids = list(text_bytes) # list of integers in range 0..255
         merge_map = build_merge_map(self.merges)
diff --git a/minbpe/regex.py b/minbpe/regex.py
--- a/minbpe/regex.py
+++ b/minbpe/regex.py
@@ -338,8 +338,7 @@ class RegexTokenizer(Tokenizer):
                 unique = list(dict.fromkeys(text_chunks))
                 s = sep.join([ch.encode("utf-8").decode("latin-1") for ch in unique])
                 for pair, new, _ in steps:
-                    if pair in s:
-                        s = s.replace(pair, new)
+                    s = s.replace(pair, new)
                 piece_of = dict(zip(unique, s.split(sep)))
                 return list(map(ord, "".join(map(piece_of.__getitem__, text_chunks))))
         # all chunks of text are encoded separately, then results are joined
